title: Software Engineers Who Only Code Are Running Out of Time
description:
At Google, 75% of all new code is generated by AI, and engineers approve it. At Anthropic, over 90% of the contributions to its own codebase in September 2026 were written by Claude. You just cannot keep your head down and write code anymore. So what is a software engineer actually getting paid for?

Code got cheap, but outcomes didn't. I show how the old pod of 6 people turns into one engineer directing AI agents, which is how I run my whole company. Then the 4 versions of the engineer on the AAARRR pirate funnel: growth, product, platform and GTM. Not one of them is defined by a programming language. Each one is defined by the outcome it owns.

And the market backs it up. Software jobs aren't disappearing, but 71% of the increase in software postings went to senior roles, and entry-level jobs are only 4.5% of them. The demand moved. Which piece of the business do you want to own?
